claims: Design Council describes discovering the problem, defining it, developing different answers and testing small-scale solutions.
Pentagram's Mastercard case study connects interlocking geometry to connection and describes color testing across backgrounds.
Blender's Bevel modifier provides width, segments, custom profiles and intersection controls.
Blender's Bump node perturbs surface normals from a height texture.
The Principled BSDF supports dielectric and metallic responses, layered coat, and roughness controlling reflection spread.

evidence.text: DISCOVER: understand rather than assume what the problem is. DEFINE: insight gathered can help define the challenge differently. DEVELOP: give different answers to clearly defined problem. DELIVER: testing different solutions at small scale, rejecting those that will not work and improving others.

The overlapping forms effortlessly express the idea of connection. The entire identity is built using core elements found in the logo: geometry and color. Getting the three colors right required hundreds of tests for different backgrounds.
Width: size of bevel effect. Segments: number of edge loops added along bevel face. Custom Profile allows user-defined profile. Intersections controls method to complete intersection mesh.
The Bump node generates a perturbed normal from a height texture, for bump mapping.

Base layer mixes metal, diffuse, subsurface and transmission components; diffuse sits below specular layer. Roughness specifies microfacet roughness for specular reflection and transmission, from sharp to diffuse reflection. Coat simulates clearcoat or lacquer on top.
